parts: Please read /investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry/notes/32_SOURCE_RELATION_COMMUTATOR_CONTINUATION_20261028.md. Please describe at a high level the approach being taken so far.
I’ll read the note and the repository’s research guidance, then explain the overall strategy and the main obstacle it is trying to resolve.

The central idea is to build an auxiliary flow in which a zero collision would force a measurable blow-up. The notes establish that mechanism; the unresolved step is finding a property of the actual theta source that prevents the blow-up. I’m checking the preceding notes to explain why the two estimates tried so far fall short.

The strategy in [Note32](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry/notes/32_SOURCE_RELATION_COMMUTATOR_CONTINUATION_20261028.md) is to **make a hypothetical zero collision force a blow-up in an auxiliary flow, then use the special structure of the theta source to prevent that blow-up**. The notes establish the first part for a particular flow. The second part remains the central open problem.

1. **Represent a collision through two conserved quantities.**  
   At a fixed physical time \(T\) and frequency \(A\), a collision means
   \[
   H(T,A)=0,\qquad H_A(T,A)=0.
   \]
   The complete theta source is represented as a radial field in three dimensions. Two components, \(U\) and its actual frequency derivative \(V\), have spatial integrals equal to those two quantities. This puts the collision condition into a form that can be studied through spatial evolution.

2. **Build a flow that amplifies simultaneous cancellation.**  
   The fields evolve in a separate auxiliary time, while \(T\) and \(A\) stay fixed. Diffusion smooths them, while an inward drift compresses them. The drift adjusts to keep their combined squared \(L^2\) norm constant, and both spatial integrals remain conserved.

   [Note28](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry/notes/28_ENERGY_NORMALIZED_CONSERVATIVE_COLLISION_MAGNIFIER_20261028.md) proves that if both integrals vanish, the gradient energy and drift strength must diverge before an explicit finite deadline. Consequently, an independent theta-specific bound keeping them finite through that deadline would exclude the collision.

3. **Test whether positivity supplies the needed bound.**  
   The first attempt surrounds the signed fields with a positive comparison density. This gives useful moment and dissipation identities. But positivity does not control the cancellations that make both integrals vanish.

   [Note29](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry/notes/29_POSITIVE_CARRIER_COMPARISON_AND_QUANTITATIVE_REGULARITY_20261028.md) obtains explicit regularity bounds when a positive lower bound on \(\sqrt{H^2+H_A^2}\) is already available. That clarifies the quantitative relationship, but it does not enlarge the region where collisions are excluded.

4. **Bring the detailed theta source into the gradient calculation.**  
   The next attempt uses the source’s logarithmic radial derivative to relate spatial derivatives to frequency derivatives. Its fixed coefficients encode the complete theta source.

   The difficulty uncovered in [Note31](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry/notes/31_CANONICAL_SOURCE_RELATION_AND_PREPARATORY_COMMUTATOR_20261028.md) is that this exact relation changes under the smoothing required to start the flow. Smoothing creates a nonzero **residual**, and subsequent evolution continually forces that residual through a **commutator**—the difference between applying the source operator before or after the evolution operator.

   The residual is essential: it cancels an apparent singularity at the unit sphere. Discarding it manufactures an infinite gradient even for smooth initial data. Extending the operator toward the origin also requires care.

5. **Seek a coupled estimate that preserves those cancellations.**  
   The current proposal is to estimate the fields, their true second frequency derivative, and the residual together. The desired inequality must control gradient growth while retaining the sphere cancellation, the interior of the unit ball, and all commutator terms.

   It must exploit a property that known [colliding control sources](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/result-summaries/12_collision_controls_and_screening.md) do not share. Simply assuming global regularity would [restate the target](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/avoid/01_restating_the_target.md), because regularity of this particular flow is already equivalent to pointwise noncollision.

The progress so far is a concrete collision-amplifying mechanism and a precise account of why two proposed bounds fall short. **The missing advance is a signed estimate specific to theta that prevents the forced blow-up.** No new theta collision exclusion or threshold bound has yet resulted; extending a successful estimate uniformly over the required physical parameters would be a further step.
First of all, please include the new results in the manuscript.
I’ll integrate the results from Notes28–29 and31 into the existing manuscript, preserving their stated scope, then compile it and update the milestone history.
